# Security review of the threat model: Phase 1 (spec 13, 23; HIMS-SEC-011)

**Reviewed:** 2026-11-11 · **Reviewer:** Internal engineering review against the threat model, spec 13 and the spec 23 security checklist. Not a substitute for the independent review and penetration test before go-live (HIMS-SEC-021).

**Scope:** Everything built in Phase 1 (the application: every API endpoint, the admin console, background jobs, uploads, backups), on a developer PC with synthetic data. Hosting (Oracle Cloud) is reviewed again when it is set up.

**Method:** Each threat-model row checked against the code and its tests; the code searched for the usual weak spots (raw SQL, unescaped HTML, missing CSRF, open redirects, unsafe file handling, secrets, debug settings); every endpoint's access rule read from the code (HIMS-DOC-001); the ten spec 13.5 security tests mapped to automated tests; dependency audits (pip-audit, npm audit).

Threats and controls: [threat-model.md](threat-model.md). Live view: the **Compliance** page, **Security review** tab, and **Security status** in the admin console.

## Findings

| Code | Severity | Area | Finding | Fix | Status | Tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-01 | medium | Sign-in sessions (13.1) | Screens that refresh themselves (Bed board, Background jobs, Rota, the confirm-it's-you status) renewed the 30-minute idle timeout, so a screen left open on a ward PC stayed signed in for ever; there was no upper limit on a session. | Background refreshes are marked by the app and no longer count as use; the server ends a session after 30 minutes without use and after 12 hours in any case (HIMS_SESSION_IDLE_SECONDS, HIMS_SESSION_MAX_SECONDS); ended sessions are audited. | fixed | `test_background_refreshes_do_not_keep_a_session_awake`<br>`test_nobody_stays_signed_in_past_the_time_limit` |
| F-02 | medium | Password guessing (13.1) | Wrong passwords were limited per client address only, so one person's password could be guessed from many addresses without slowing down. | Wrong passwords are also counted per email: after 10 within 15 minutes, sign-in with that email pauses for 15 minutes in the app and the console, with the same answer for emails that have no account. | fixed | `test_wrong_passwords_pause_sign_in_for_that_email_from_any_address`<br>`test_console_sign_in_shares_the_per_account_pause` |
| F-03 | low | Encryption keys (13.3) | A new encryption key could be added, but nothing encrypted the stored secrets again, so an old key could never be retired. | `rotate_encryption_keys` encrypts every stored secret again with the newest key (audited); the Compliance page and the console show how many values still need an older key. | fixed | `test_old_encryption_keys_can_be_retired_after_rotation` |
| F-04 | low | Audit log flooding (13.4) | Any signed-in account could call the "no access yet" report up to 1,200 times a minute, each writing an audit event that can never be deleted. | One event per person per 10 minutes (the same reference is returned); someone who already has access records nothing. | fixed | `test_no_access_reports_cannot_flood_the_audit_log` |
| F-05 | low | Background jobs (13.5) | A background event was processed without checking which hospital it belongs to; queues are separate per deployment, but a shared broker or a copied database could run another hospital's work here. | Messages carry the deployment and are refused when it differs; an event whose own hospital is not this deployment is marked failed with the reason and never runs. | fixed | `test_a_background_event_for_another_hospital_never_runs` |
| F-06 | info | Dependencies | npm audit lists 10 moderate advisories (minimatch, a pattern-matching library) in the lint tools only; nothing in the app that browsers download. The fix would move ESLint back a major version. | Accepted: lint tools never reach a hospital. CI blocks high advisories in the shipped packages; Dependabot proposes the fixed version when ESLint releases one. | accepted | — |
| F-07 | info | Threat model | The threat model still listed built controls (content security policy, passkeys, the secret-in-logs test, restore drills) as gaps. | Threat model brought up to date and marked reviewed; the remaining gaps point at their tickets. | fixed | — |

## Checked and found sound

| Area | What was checked |
|---|---|
| Forged requests | Every signed-in write goes through CSRF checks; the nine sign-in, invitation and reset endpoints that run before sign-in enforce CSRF themselves. |
| Injection | No SQL built from user input: the few raw statements use fixed names or quoted identifiers; no `eval`, `pickle`, unsafe YAML or shell commands. |
| Cross-site scripting | React escapes all text and nothing uses raw HTML; the two server-side HTML spots escape first; content security policy on screens, console and API. |
| Access control | Default deny on every endpoint, read from the code and pinned by tests (HIMS-DOC-001); only 12 endpoints work without sign-in, all rate limited; rows outside a facility grant answer 404. |
| Files | Uploads are virus-checked, typed by content and size-limited; downloads need a permission and the person's scope, are audited, and are sent as attachments with a sandbox policy and no caching. |
| Secrets | Nothing secret in the repository (secret scan in CI), logs, traces or audit metadata (tests); hosted settings refuse to start without their keys; API docs and the console are off unless switched on, the console only from allowed addresses. |
| Transport and browser | HTTPS redirect, HSTS, secure and HTTP-only cookies, SameSite, X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, strict referrer policy in hosted settings; checked by `check --deploy` in CI. |
| Sign-in | Argon2 password hashing, 12-character minimum and common-password checks, the same answer for unknown and wrong accounts, session key renewed at sign-in, two-factor for privileged roles (enforced in production), confirm-it's-you for 23 sensitive actions. |
| Dependencies | pip-audit: no known vulnerabilities; npm audit of shipped packages: none; libraries hash-locked, GitHub Actions pinned to commits. |

## The ten security tests of spec 13.5

| # | Case | Status | How | Tests |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A user from Hospital A requests a patient ID belonging to Hospital B. | Tested for Phase 1 records; patients follow | Each hospital has its own deployment and database (ADR-003) with its own cookies; an ID or a session from elsewhere is simply not there. Patients arrive in Phase 2 on the same basis. | `apps/compliance/tests/test_security_review.py::test_a_record_or_session_from_another_hospital_is_not_found`<br>`common/tests/test_environment.py::test_deployment_identity_required` |
| 2 | A doctor accesses a patient outside the authorized scope. | Tested for Phase 1 records; patients follow | Facility and department scope on every list and record (staff, beds, rota); patient and encounter scope with Phase 2 (HIMS-IAM-010). | `apps/staff/tests/test_directory_scope.py::test_someone_elsewhere_is_not_found_and_changes_stay_hospital_wide`<br>`apps/beds/tests/test_bed_board.py::test_a_department_grant_sees_only_its_wards` |
| 3 | A nurse attempts to modify a signed doctor's note. | Waits for the feature | Clinical notes are Phase 2 (slice 2C); the test is written with them. | — |
| 4 | A pharmacist attempts to dispense more stock than is available. | Waits for the feature | Pharmacy is Phase 4; the test is written with it. | — |
| 5 | A terminated employee reuses an old session. | Tested | Ending employment ends every session on every device; the next request is refused. | `apps/identity/tests/test_sessions.py::test_terminating_staff_signs_them_out_on_every_device` |
| 6 | A user downloads a document by guessing another document's URL. | Tested | Document addresses are random IDs and every download checks the permission and the person's scope; a guessed address answers 404. | `apps/compliance/tests/test_security_review.py::test_a_guessed_document_address_finds_nothing` |
| 7 | A Celery job runs with missing or stale customer context. | Tested | Queues per deployment; messages carry the deployment; events of another hospital are refused and marked failed (finding F-05). | `apps/compliance/tests/test_security_review.py::test_a_background_event_for_another_hospital_never_runs` |
| 8 | A report export includes patients outside the authorized facility. | Tested for Phase 1 records; patients follow | Phase 1 lists follow the facility and department scope; the only exports (audit log, access reviews) are hospital-wide by design and need confirm-it's-you. Patient reports come with Phase 2 (HIMS-RPT). | `apps/staff/tests/test_directory_scope.py::test_licence_expiry_list_follows_the_same_scope` |
| 9 | An integration logs a secret or sensitive patient data during an exception. | Tested | The real flows run and the logs, audit log, stored errors and responses are searched for every secret. | `common/tests/test_secrets_never_logged.py::test_no_secret_reaches_a_log_the_audit_log_or_a_stored_error` |
| 10 | A database restore recovers records but fails to restore required audit relationships. | Tested | The restore drill checks the audit chain and its links; a copy that lost them fails. | `apps/recovery/tests/test_restore_drill.py::test_restore_that_loses_audit_relationships_is_caught` |
